note: Photoreal mp4s are optional. HTML/SVG labels are exam-accurate. verified:false until a human checks Imagine frames. Do not treat generated text in a frame as a pinout or URL.

assets.prompt: Deterministic CSS — orange/green pair swap only. Pins 1-8 numbered in HTML. Not Imagine.
assets.alt: T568A versus T568B with numbered pins and pair swap
assets.transcript: T568A and T568B use the same eight pin numbers. Only the orange and green pairs swap. Pins 4-5 stay blue and 7-8 stay brown. Same standard on both ends is a straight-through cable.

assets.prompt: Deterministic CSS — RAID 0 stripe versus RAID 1 copy then one disk FAIL. RAID is not a backup. Not Imagine.
assets.alt: RAID 0 loses the volume on one fail; RAID 1 stays degraded
assets.transcript: RAID 0 stripes A1 and A2 across two disks. Fail disk 2 and the volume is empty. RAID 1 copies A1 to both disks. Fail disk 2 and A1 is still on disk 1. That is redundancy, not a backup.

assets.prompt: Deterministic CSS — three labeled circles 2.4 largest, 6 GHz smallest. No heatmap. Not Imagine.
assets.transcript: 2.4 GHz travels farthest and collides more. 5 GHz is shorter and cleaner. 6 GHz is smallest and needs Wi-Fi 6E radios on both the AP and the client.

assets.prompt: Deterministic CSS terminal — DHCP fails then one IPv4 line 169.254.x.x. Not a Windows screenshot.
assets.transcript: When DHCP does not answer, Windows assigns a link-local APIPA address in 169.254.0.0/16. There is no useful default gateway. Limited connectivity is a DHCP or cable problem, not a DNS first step.

assets.prompt: Deterministic CSS — HDMI, DisplayPort, VGA each seat only in the matching port. USB-A trident-up, USB-C either way.
assets.alt: Matching video plugs and USB orientation
assets.transcript: HDMI, DisplayPort, and VGA are keyed differently. A plug that is not the matching port lifts back out. USB-A seats trident-up. USB-C seats either way. USB-C is a shell, not a protocol.

assets.prompt: Deterministic CSS — inkjet cartridge versus laser toner slide-in. Do not animate the 7-step laser process.
assets.alt: Inkjet ink and laser toner cartridges sliding into bays
assets.transcript: Inkjet uses liquid ink cartridges. Laser uses a toner cartridge of charged powder. This clip only shows seating. The seven-step laser imaging process stays on the still diagram.

assets.prompt: Deterministic CSS — 3.5-inch and 2.5-inch HDD outlines next to a millimeter ruler.
assets.alt: 3.5 inch and 2.5 inch drives beside a ruler
assets.transcript: 3.5-inch drives are desktop and NAS bays. 2.5-inch drives are laptops and some caddies. Form factor is size, not SSD versus spinning rust. If the ticket mentions rpm, it is an HDD.

assets.prompt: Deterministic CSS — webcam LED on, shutter closes, LED off.
assets.alt: Laptop webcam privacy shutter covering the lens
assets.transcript: A privacy shutter is a physical cover the operating system cannot override. When the shutter is open the webcam LED can light. When the shutter closes, the LED goes off. Do not start with a Windows reinstall.

assets.prompt: Photoreal bench, 6 seconds, one motion, no UI chrome, no glowing internals. Hands seat a 24-pin ATX into a desktop motherboard, then an 8-pin EPS CPU power. Do not bake labels into the frame.
assets.transcript: The 24-pin ATX connector powers the board. The 8-pin EPS connector near the CPU socket is required on modern boards. Both must fully seat. Labels are HTML overlays, not video text.

assets.prompt: Photoreal bench, 6 seconds, one motion. DDR DIMM aligned to the notch; both latches close. No labels in the frame.
assets.transcript: Align the DIMM notch to the slot. Press evenly until both side latches close. Do not force a different DDR generation. Overlay says DIMM.

assets.prompt: Photoreal bench, 6 seconds. SODIMM at 30 degrees then flat in a laptop slot, next to a larger DIMM for scale. No labels in the frame.
assets.alt: SODIMM angled install beside a DIMM
assets.transcript: A SODIMM starts at an angle, then presses flat until the clips catch. A desktop DIMM is about twice as long and does not belong in a laptop slot.

assets.prompt: Photoreal bench, 6 seconds. M.2 card at an angle, one screw. No labels in the frame.
assets.alt: M.2 card secured with one screw
assets.transcript: M.2 is the slot form factor. NVMe is the protocol that usually rides PCIe on that slot. Seat the card at an angle and fasten the one screw. Read the board legend for SATA versus NVMe wiring.

assets.prompt: Photoreal bench, 6 seconds. Thin SATA data versus wide SATA power, both click. No labels in the frame.
assets.alt: SATA data and SATA power connectors seating
assets.transcript: SATA data is the thin L-shaped cable. SATA power is the wider 15-pin cable. Both click. They are not interchangeable with Molex without an adapter.

assets.prompt: Photoreal bench, 6 seconds. RJ45 into a jack until the tab clicks; cut to a crimper on a plug. No tester LCD numbers. No labels in the frame.
assets.transcript: Push an RJ45 into a jack until the tab clicks. Building a patch cord uses a crimper after the conductors are in T568 order. Do not invent tester LCD numbers from a generated frame.

assets.prompt: Photoreal bench, 6 seconds. Wrist strap, clip on unpainted chassis metal. No labels in the frame.
assets.alt: ESD wrist strap clipped to unpainted chassis
assets.transcript: An ESD wrist strap connects you to ground through a resistor. Clip it to unpainted chassis metal or a grounded mat. Painted metal is not a ground. Self-grounding is a weak substitute.

assets.prompt: Photoreal bench, 6 seconds. Tower PC into a small UPS, UPS into wall, LED on battery. No labels in the frame.
assets.alt: PC into UPS into wall with on-battery LED
assets.transcript: The PC plugs into the UPS. The UPS plugs into the wall. On a blackout the LED shows on battery so you can shut down cleanly. A surge strip is not a UPS and does nothing for a brownout.

assets.prompt: Photoreal bench, 6 seconds. Three trays Degauss / Wipe / Shred; a drive goes to shred, platters destroyed. No labels in the frame.
assets.alt: HDD moving to the shred tray
assets.transcript: Shredding destroys platters so the drive cannot be reused. Degaussing is for magnetic media, not SSD. Wipe is for reuse. RAID is not a destruction method.

assets.prompt: Photoreal bench, 6 seconds. Fake email; do not bake URL spelling into the frame. HTML overlays supply paypal.com versus paypa1-secure.example.
assets.alt: Email hover showing displayed text versus real URL
assets.transcript: The friendly text can say paypal.com while the real URL is paypa1-secure.example. Trust the HTML overlay strings in this academy, not any spelling Imagine draws inside a frame.
